set.body:
Objective:
Define Frame semantics independently of every optional engine and implement the always-available vectorized reference interpreter over scoped record batches.

Semantic constitution:
- SQL-style three-valued logic; filters retain only true.
- Null equality, null-safe equality, grouping of null keys, NaN behavior, integer overflow, casts, timestamp units/zones, dictionary equality, collation, sort stability, and floating reduction policy are explicit.
- There is no hidden row index. Keys are ordinary columns. Order is represented by an inspectable OrderGuarantee and preserved only by operators whose contract says so.
- Backend equivalence means these semantics, with any permitted floating-order tolerance declared in the plan or receipt.

Local engine boundary:
- Own the minimal relational kernels required for Boolean logic, validity, comparisons, casts, hashing, grouping keys, strings/dictionaries, sorting, and scalar aggregates.
- Do not depend on Gale or ScalaFIM. General linear algebra remains outside Frame.
- Operators pull and emit batches through an explicit resource-safe protocol; project, filter, and limit stream without whole-input materialization.
- Blocking behavior and memory estimates are inspectable before execution.

Acceptance:
- Project, filter, limit, expression evaluation, null handling, and baseline reductions execute on JVM and Scala.js.
- Deterministic fixtures and property laws cover three-valued logic, filter composition, projection identity, ordering guarantees, chunk-boundary invariance, checked arithmetic, and structured failures.
- Explain output distinguishes logical, optimized, and physical stages even before the optimizer gains rewrite rules.
- No engine silently changes semantics or falls back to another backend.
- Performance receipts cover representative primitive and UTF-8 batch paths without making unmeasured parity claims.
set.title: Frame foundation 3: semantic constitution and independent local reference engine
